Do not include private or machine-specific details in the PR, such as a local username.

## One-Line Summary
<!--
Summarize this PR in one sentence from the user's perspective.
Focus on the concrete pain it removes or the behavior it improves, not an abstract goal.
-->

## User-Facing Changes
<!--
Avoid vague wording.
Quote actual error messages or UI text when relevant, and describe observable scenario-level changes as flat bullet points.
-->

## Why This Changed
<!--
Explain the structural limitation in the previous design and how it caused confusion, breakage, or friction.
Do not stop at symptoms; make the causal chain explicit.
-->

## How It Changed
<!--
Describe the important implementation changes, not generic architecture language.
Include the main state names, patterns, fallback handling, or background behavior when those matter.
Use flat bullet points to show how data and state now flow.
-->

## Bug Fixes
<!--
Avoid broad statements.
List concrete symptoms in the form "under X timing/condition, Y incorrect behavior happened, and this change fixes or mitigates it."
Delete this section if it does not apply.
-->

## Performance Notes (Optional)
<!--
Delete this section if there is no performance-related change.
If included, state what unnecessary work was removed and which metric or user-visible latency improved.
-->

## Extra Context / Decisions (Optional)
<!--
Delete this section if there are no noteworthy tradeoffs or technical decisions to share with reviewers.
If needed, keep it brief.
-->

## Verification
<!--
Avoid vague statements like "tests passed."
List the actual commands you ran.
If you added or changed tests, name the files and describe the exact scenarios or state transitions they cover.
-->

## Video / Screenshot (Optional)
<!--
Attach media for visible UI/UX changes.
If this PR only changes internal logic, write N/A.
-->
